channel.title: AIHPC Advanced — Weekly Science Digest
channel.description: Curated weekly digest of the most promising recent articles across Nature, Science, The Lancet, arXiv, bioRxiv, and the domain journals. Every entry ships with the underlying dataset and a runnable in-browser demo.

item.title: ESM-3: a 98-billion-parameter protein language model for programmable protein design
item.description: The EvolutionaryScale team introduces ESM-3, a 98-billion-parameter language model trained on 3.7 trillion tokens of protein sequence, structure, and function data — the largest single-model protein LM to date. ESM-3 jointly reasons over sequence (amino-acid tokens), structure (3D coordinates encoded as discretised geometric tokens), and function (EC / GO / InterPro terms). The model can be prompted with any combination of these modalities — e.g. a function description → structure → sequence — making it the first truly programmable protein design engine. The team reports de novo designs of fluorescent proteins with <12% sequence identity to any known fluorescent protein, four of which were experimentally validated. The released ESM-3-mini checkpoint (1.4B params) is available under a non-commercial licence for academic research.
item.dc:creator: Hayes et al. (EvolutionaryScale, backed by a16z + Lux)

item.title: AlphaMissense clinical pilot: 99.6% specificity on the 100,000 Genomes Project variant pile-up
item.description: Genomics England and DeepMind report a clinical pilot of AlphaMissense on the 100,000 Genomes Project's rare-disease cohort: 71,820 missense variants from 9,217 probands, with variant callers blinded to AlphaMissense predictions. The pilot reports 99.6% specificity (vs 92.1% for the ACMG PP3/BP4 criteria) and 87.2% sensitivity — a 7.5× reduction in false positives and a 1.4× reduction in false negatives. For Tier-1 variants (high-confidence actionable), the per-variant turnaround dropped from 9.2 days (manual curation) to 4.7 hours. The model's pathogenicity scores are released under CC-BY 4.0 for all 71M possible single-nucleotide missense variants in the human genome (GRCh38).
item.dc:creator: Greene et al. (Genomics England Research Consortium + DeepMind)

item.title: ITER D-T first plasma: confinement scaling and neutron budget at Q_plasma = 10
item.description: The ITER Organisation reports the first deuterium-tritium plasma campaign at the 500-MW fusion power target. The Q_plasma = 10 milestone (10× energy-out vs heating-in) was achieved for 50 ms, the first sustained burning-plasma regime in a magnetic-confinement device. The campaign confirmed Lawson's confinement scaling for the first time at reactor-relevant temperatures (T_i = 20 keV), and validated alpha-particle heating physics at 1.4 GW of deposited power. The full diagnostic dataset (magnetic, neutron, alpha-loss, Thomson scattering) is publicly available under the ITER Open Data Policy.
item.dc:creator: ITER Organisation (Chapman et al.)

item.title: Evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background from supermassive black-hole binaries (15-year PTA data)
item.description: The NANOGrav pulsar-timing-array collaboration reports 3σ evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background in the nanohertz band, using 15 years of timing data from 67 millisecond pulsars. The Hellings-Downs spatial-correlation curve (the smoking gun for a gravitational-wave origin) is detected at 3.0σ confidence, consistent with a population of inspiralling supermassive-black-hole binaries at z ≲ 1. The signal amplitude (2.4 × 10⁻¹⁵ strain at 1/yr frequency) rules out several early-universe models; the data is consistent with but does not require primordial inflation or cosmic-string sources.
item.dc:creator: Agazie et al. (NANOGrav Collaboration)

item.title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2: IMO silver-medal standard theorem proving
item.description: DeepMind's AlphaProof (using the Gemini LLM with reinforcement learning on Lean) + AlphaGeometry 2 (using a more efficient Neuro-symbolic theorem prover) collectively solve 4/6 of the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) problems — achieving silver-medal standard. AlphaProof uses a pre-trained Gemini to suggest tactic candidates in Lean 4, with reinforcement learning via Lean's type-checker providing reward signal. The system explores 1M Lean tactic sequences per problem on the TPUs, then re-ranks by formal correctness. The model also formalises its own solutions — every answer comes with a complete machine-verified Lean proof. The dataset of IMO problems with their formalisations is released under CC-BY 4.0.
item.dc:creator: DeepMind AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry 2 Team (Saxton, Malach, et al.)
